questions.question_text:
A loan of $\$18\,000$ at $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($r=0.005$) is repaid with $\$350$ per month.
How many whole monthly repayments are required to pay off the loan?

options.why: Rounded down to 59, leaving an unpaid balance.
Reported a fractional number of repayments instead of a whole number.
Ignored interest and rounded $18\,000/350=51.428571\ldots$ up to $52$ repayments.

questions.question_text:
A borrower owes $\$30\,000$ on a line of credit charging $12\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($r=0.01$).
If repayments are set to $\$280$ per month, what will happen to the loan?

options.text: The loan will never be repaid because the monthly repayment is less than the monthly interest charge of $\$300$.
The loan will be repaid in $108$ months.
options.why: Ignored interest and rounded $30\,000/280=107.142857\ldots$ up to $108$ months.

options.text: The loan balance will remain constant at $\$30\,000$.
options.why: Assumed the repayment matches the interest exactly.

options.text: The loan will be repaid in $1500$ months.
options.why: Treated the first month's balance increase of $\$20$ as a fixed principal reduction and calculated $30\,000/20=1500$ months.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Monthly interest}=30\,000\times0.01=\$300$
Since the $\$280$ repayment is less than the $\$300$ interest, the debt grows each month and the loan is never repaid.

questions.question_text:
A loan of $\$60\,000$ at $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($r=0.005$) has standard repayments of $\$600$ per month ($139$ months).
If repayments are increased to $\$800$ per month, how many months earlier is the loan paid off?

options.why: Reported the new loan term instead of the time saved.
Treated the repayment increase of $\$200$ as a time saving of $200$ months.
Subtracted the fractional new term from $139$, giving $44.7645\ldots$ months, instead of first rounding the new repayment count up to $95$.

questions.question_text:
A debt of $\$10\,000$ at $9\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($r=0.0075$) is repaid at $\$250$ per month.
What is the value of $(1.0075)^{n}$ when $A_{n}=0$?

options.why: Divided repayment by principal instead of solving the geometric series equation.
Reported the annual growth factor $1+0.09=1.09$ instead of isolating $(1.0075)^n$.
Inverted the fraction in the logarithmic argument.

questions.question_text:
A loan of $\$20\,000$ at $12\%$ p.a. compounded monthly is repaid with $\$900$ at the end of each month. Its theoretical term is $n=\dfrac{\log(9/7)}{\log1.01}=25.2568\ldots$ months.
Calculate the smaller final repayment on month $26$, to the nearest cent.

options.why: Used the balance after payment $25$ without adding the interest for month $26$.
Charged a full regular repayment instead of clearing only the remaining balance and its final month's interest.
Applied one month's interest to the original principal and ignored all $25$ repayments.

questions.solution_text:
$A_{25}=20\,000(1.01)^{25}-900\left[\dfrac{(1.01)^{25}-1}{0.01}\right]\approx\$229.76$
Using the unrounded balance, $\text{Final payment}=A_{25}(1.01)\approx\$232.06$ to the nearest cent.

questions.question_text:
A loan of $\$30\,000$ charges $12\%$ p.a. compounded monthly. Repayments of $\$600$ are made at the end of each month.
How many whole monthly repayments are needed to pay off the loan?

options.why: Rounded the theoretical term $69.6607\ldots$ down, leaving an unpaid balance.
Ignored interest and calculated $30\,000/600=50$ repayments.
Treated the first month's principal reduction of $\$300$ as constant and calculated $30\,000/300=100$ repayments.

questions.solution_text:
$r=0.12/12=0.01$
$A_n=30\,000(1.01)^n-600(1.01)^{n-1}-\cdots-600$
Summing the repayment geometric series gives $A_n=30\,000(1.01)^n-600\left[\dfrac{(1.01)^n-1}{0.01}\right]$.
Set $A_n=0$: $(1.01)^n=\dfrac{600}{600-30\,000(0.01)}=2$.
$n=\dfrac{\log2}{\log1.01}=69.6607\ldots$, so $70$ repayments are needed.

questions.question_text:
An investor borrows $\$120\,000$ at $4.8\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($r=0.004$).
If they repay $\$1000$ per month, find the exact number of whole monthly repayments needed to clear the debt.

options.why: Rounded down to 163, leaving the final partial debt unpaid.
Assumed $\$1000$ per month pays off $\$120\,000$ in 120 months without interest.
Added another repayment after already rounding the theoretical term up to $164$.

questions.question_text:
A loan of $\$10\,000$ at $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($r=0.005$) is repaid with $\$400$ per month ($n=26.77$ months).
What is the final payment on month $27$, to the nearest cent?

options.why: Calculated $0.77 \times \$400$ without compounding the remaining balance.
Omitted interest accrued in the 27th month on the remaining balance.
Charged a full standard repayment on the final month.

questions.solution_text:
$A_{26}=10\,000(1.005)^{26}-400\left[\dfrac{(1.005)^{26}-1}{0.005}\right]\approx\$307.83$
Using the unrounded value of $A_{26}$, $\text{Final payment}=A_{26}(1.005)\approx\$309.37$ to the nearest cent.
